subject.title: fix(diagnostics): scale heap pressure thresholds relative to V8 heap size limit

question: Should critical memory pressure retain an absolute 3 GiB RSS ceiling, or should RSS also scale with host/cgroup capacity so enlarged V8 heaps can use proportional heap thresholds without an earlier RSS critical event?
rationale: The heap-only patch cannot determine the product’s complete pressure policy because the existing RSS branch independently selects critical pressure first.

options.title: Scale the complete pressure model
options.body: Define and test coordinated heap and RSS thresholds from V8 plus host or cgroup capacity so large-memory deployments avoid false critical events.

options.title: Keep RSS absolute
options.body: Retain 3 GiB RSS as intentionally critical and narrow this PR’s scope and claims to heap diagnostic classification rather than eliminating critical pressure.

recommendation.title: Scale the complete pressure model
recommendation.body: Define and test coordinated heap and RSS thresholds from V8 plus host or cgroup capacity so large-memory deployments avoid false critical events.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work introduced the current threshold policy, pressure ordering, and regression tests.
